h: Planes, Parks and a Proper West London Day
p: Hobbledown Heath works best when you treat it as a full outing rather than a quick pop-in. Small children can easily fill a morning between the animals and the play areas, and the storybook theme gives them something to chat about all the way home. With little ones, pick a couple of must-see animals at the start and let the rest of the day flow from there, with breaks in between for snacks and a sit-down. Sturdy shoes beat sandals, even in summer.

One of the joys of the location is how much greenery sits around it, despite the busy roads and the airport. Hounslow Heath has a rich mix of heathland and grassland, and it's a surprisingly peaceful place to walk off lunch. A short drive away, Osterley Park, run by the National Trust, has a grand Georgian house, gardens and acres of parkland where the kids can run free. Syon Park, on the Thames near Brentford, is another big country estate on the doorstep of the city.

If you're making a weekend of it, Kew Gardens is only a few miles east, perfect for older kids and adults who fancy something gentler the next day, with the treetop walkway and huge glasshouses to explore. Twickenham and Richmond are close too, with riverside walks and plenty of places to eat. For families coming from further afield, being so close to the M4 and M25 means it's often easier to reach than you'd think. Plane spotters, meanwhile, will want to keep one eye on the sky the entire time.
